Sensitivity is the proportion of people with the condition that test positive.  So the first we need to find out how many people had the condition that tested positive for the new diagnostic method.  From the information given we know that 48 out of 180 people had the condition. We are also told that 60 people tested positive for the condition using the new diagnostic method. Assuming that everyone who tested positive for the condition actually had the condition, then we can assume that 60 out of 48 people had the condition that tested positive for the new diagnostic method.  So we can work out the sensitivity by dividing 48 by 60 which gives us 0.8.  However, the question states that only 37 out of the 60 people who tested positive for the condition actually had the condition. So we can work out the sensitivity by dividing 37 by 48 which gives us 0.77.

The lateral corticospinal tract is the only motor pathway derived from the cerebral cortex. It is the lateral motor pathway which decussates in the pyramids of the medulla. It provides unilateral innervation to the contralateral side of the body and has a pyramidal or direct, non-reciprocal, point-to-point nature. It can be further divided into the 10th and 8th spinal segments (distal limb) and the 1st-7th segments (proximal limb). The 10th and 8th segments form the lateral (distal) motor system which provides highly fractionated, discrete, and rapid control of movements at individual digits and joints. The 1st-7th segments form the medial (proximal) motor system which provides co-activation of muscle groups to control gross movements of the upper and lower limbs.

Selectins are a transmembrane protein family that help slow the extreemly fast neutrophils down, hence the term rolling. Integrins are also:putative adhesion molecules, but their main role is in firm adhesion of the neutrophils to the vessel wall. Remember selectins bring about the rolling and integrins are responsible for the firm adhesion. Some other cells that use these same integrins include platelets. Remember platelets don't roll, they just stick! Remember that the activation of integrins is enhanced by chemokines. The fact that the integrins are enhanced by chemokines helps explain the transmigration of the neutrophils by the chemokines that drew them to the site of inflammation. See the PCS unit 1 'Wound Healing and Inflammation' plenary for more detail.

Answer: C  The sodium ion voltage gated channel has two gates, an activation and an inactivation gate. The activation gate opens rapidly in response to an increase in voltage, whilst the inactivation gate responds more slowly. During repetitive firing, the inactivation gate will close, and the cell must repolarise fully before it can reopen. This results in a period of incomplete excitability known as accommodation.

Type I pneumocytes make up 95% of the alveolar surface and are flat ciliated epithelial cells. They are involved in gas exchange.Type II pneumocytes make up 5% of the alveolar surface, are ciliated cuboidal epithelial cells and produce surfactant. There is also an  Alveolar macrophage, which engulfs pathogens and cellular debris, and Goblet cells, which secrete a serous product containing defensins, proteases and lactoferrin.
